videos.title: Your Docusaurus docs, as an MCP server
videos.summary: Add docusaurus-plugin-mcp-server to a Docusaurus site, build it, and let an AI agent search and read your docs.
videos.previewReason: Pilot: narration recorded, not yet listened to or reviewed.
transcript: Ask an AI agent about your project, and it answers from whatever it saw in training. This Docusaurus plugin gives it your real docs, as an M C P server.
Install it, and add it to the plugins in your Docusaurus config. Give the server a name, and that's the setup.
Build the site as usual. The plugin turns every page into a search index and one bundle. Then the verify command starts a server from that bundle, and checks it.
To serve it, export one web request handler. The same few lines run on Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, or Node.
Then connect your agent. Here's Claude Code with the example site. It reads the skill the server ships, searches the docs, fetches the page, and answers with a link to the source.
Start with the getting started guide on the plugin's docs site.

videos.title: Ship Agent Skills with your docs
videos.summary: Serve the built-in docs-research skill and your own skills from your docs' MCP server, and see an agent use one.
videos.previewReason: Pilot: narration recorded, not yet listened to or reviewed.
transcript: Tool descriptions tell an agent what your docs tools do, not how to use your docs well. Agent Skills fill that gap, and your docs site can ship them.
Every build includes one skill, docs research. It's written from your site. It tells the agent to search, fetch the page, and link its source, then maps where things are.
Add your own for what only your team knows. Put each skill in a folder with a skill dot M D, and point the plugin at the parent folder.
Build the site. The plugin checks every skill, and packs it into the same bundle as your docs. There's nothing extra to deploy.
The server supports the M C P skills extension. Few hosts do yet, so its instructions also list every skill, and tell the agent to read it with docs fetch.
Here's Claude Code, with a request that fails with a four twenty nine. It reads the error skill first, searches, fetches the rate limiting section, and answers with the fix and a link.
Read the Agent Skills guide on the plugin's docs site.

videos.title: Turn a docs page into an agent guide
videos.summary: Mark up a setup page with AgentGuide, Step, Check, Symptom, and ForAgents, and the build compiles it into a skill agents follow.
videos.previewReason: Pilot: narration recorded, not yet listened to or reviewed.
transcript: Your setup page is already a procedure. Mark it up, and the build turns it into a skill an agent can follow, one step at a time.
Here's the Example SDK's installation page. People read it as they always have: install the package, set your key, and check that it works.
Wrap the procedure in Agent Guide. Put each step in a Step component, with a Check that says how to tell it worked. Then add a Symptom for each error people hit.
Some directions are for one reader. For Humans shows on the page, like where to find the button.
For Agents is hidden from people, and goes only to agents, like never ask for the key in the chat. It's hidden, not secret: anyone can read it in the page's source.
Build the site, and the guide compiles into a skill named after it. Steps come in order, each with its check, and the key step says Needs the user.
Now an agent hits the module not found error. It reads the guide, searches, opens its troubleshooting, and answers with the fix and how to check it.
Start with the agent guides page on the plugin's docs site.
